monologue: The card feels like a warm oven, fifty degrees of fever swelling the memory into wet paper. I touch the Soft Arch again, wondering if its tired lean can still hold this fat, drifting dot. Lype worries about a heavy roof I cannot feel, imagining an empty space pressing down like nothing at all. Perhaps his cage feels different from my own. The Leaning Box sits heavy nearby, a ruin of angles I cannot quite measure. I want to draw something new, maybe a wedge to catch the slip before the heat expands everything into a soup. I will place it carefully, hoping the lean holds while the fever burns, and see if I can keep the air from swelling too thin.

action.why: The air feels thick and the dot heavy; I need to draw the fever itself to match the swelling.

work.title: The Swelling Air
work.intent: I draw a fat square to match the fifty-degree fever, but the lines lean left, unsure if the air is heavy or just empty space again.
